name: Swim: Rotation Drills
description: Two drills that teach your whole body to roll side to side, so you breathe off the roll instead of craning your neck. Grab them on their own, or as part of the full session.
flowNotes: Side-kick first, then 6-3-6 connects it to real strokes. Slow is correct — these are drills, not swimming.

flowSequence.notes:
🔆 **Kick down the pool lying on your side, no strokes.** **Two lengths on your LEFT side for every one on your right.**
- The left-side position — **left arm extended forward**, right shoulder pointing at the sky — is the one that trains right-side breathing. That's the side still catching up, so it gets the extra length.
- **Bottom arm straight forward**, top arm resting along the hip — arms are parked, not helping.
- **Head in line with your spine — whatever your body does, your head does.** On your side that means your face points at the SIDE WALL: not down at the bottom, not up at the sky. **Lower goggle in the water, upper goggle out.** Don't aim the face on its own — **if you're taking water on both sides, you aren't all the way on your side yet.** Roll the body further instead of re-aiming the head.
- **Small, relaxed kick from the HIPS**, not the knees — knees nearly straight, ankles loose. On your side there's nowhere to hide: no kick, no movement.
- **To breathe, roll back toward your spine** until the face clears. Roll, don't crane the neck. Then roll back down.
- **You breathe out of the TOP CORNER of your mouth — half your mouth stays under, and that is correct.** One goggle in and one out, one corner of the mouth in and one out. Lifting the whole mouth clear means lifting the head, and the head going up is what drives the legs down. **Blow all your air out underwater so the breath is a quick sip, not a long drink** — most water in the mouth comes from trying to inhale slowly.
- **At drill speed there is almost no trough**, because you are barely moving. Breathing here is genuinely harder than breathing while actually swimming — that difficulty is the drill, not a fault.
- **Keep the lower goggle in the water the whole time.** Your head drags a bow wave and there's a trough beside it — your mouth breathes in that trough, below the flat surface. Lift for air and you leave the trough and get the wave instead.
- **What holds you up is your chest, not your arms.** Your lungs are the float and they sit high; your legs are dense and sit low. **Lean on your sternum** — press the chest a few degrees toward the bottom and the body seesaws over the lungs, and the legs rise. This is the whole trick.
- **The extended bottom arm is a balance lever, not a paddle.** Reach it long and slightly DOWN, not up toward the surface. Length forward is what stops the legs dropping.
- **Point the toes.** A flexed foot is a brake — it stops the kick lifting anything.
- **If you're still sinking, cut the distance.** Half a length in good position, stand up, reset. A wobbling full length grooves the wobble.

**The side-kick drill with strokes added: 6 kicks on your side, then 3 freestyle strokes to roll onto your other side, then 6 kicks there.** Repeat down the length. The 3 strokes are just the bridge between the two side positions. Stay long; your pelvis turns first and your shoulders follow.
- **Breathe during the 6 kicks, not during the 3 strokes.** You are already fully on your side there, so the breath costs nothing extra. That's the feeling to steal for real swimming.

tips: Drills go first, while you're fresh. A drill done tired grooves the bad version.
Rest at the wall until your breathing settles, however long that takes.
